The test image shows a tomato compound leaf with:
- Large, irregular dark brown-black necrotic lesions at leaflet margins/tips
- Yellow-green chlorotic halos surrounding the dark necrotic areas
- Bilateral symmetry of damage on left and right leaflets

This pattern (large marginal necrosis with yellow halo) is most consistent with **Late Blight** or **Early Blight**. Let me view a Late Blight reference to confirm.

The Late Blight reference confirms the pattern: large irregular dark necrotic areas spreading from leaf margins with surrounding chlorosis. The test image matches this presentation well — dark brown-black marginal necrosis with yellow-green halos on a tomato compound leaf, typical of *Phytophthora infestans* (Late Blight) early-to-mid stage infection.

Early Blight would show concentric ring "target board" patterns rather than this large, irregular marginal necrosis. The lesion morphology here (dark, irregular, margin-starting) rules it out.
